title: Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman named deputy director of NASA JPL
excerpt: The former astronaut will begin his new role at the Southern California laboratory on November 30, 2026.
bodyHtml:
NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory announced on October 28, 2026, that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman has been appointed as the deputy director of the laboratory and an associate vice president at Caltech. Wiseman, an emeritus astronaut and retired U.S. Navy captain, is scheduled to begin his new position on November 30, 2026.

In his new capacity, Wiseman will be responsible for the strategic leadership, stewardship, and continuous improvement of laboratory operations. He will also serve as the Center Management Authority for mission execution and act as the primary interface for national security programs at the facility.

Wiseman previously served as the agency’s chief astronaut from December 2020 to November 2022. During his career, he also served as flight engineer aboard the International Space Station for the 165-day Expedition 41 mission in 2014 and was a commander of NASA’s 21st Extreme Environment Mission Operations expedition in 2016.

Wiseman holds a bachelor’s degree in computer and systems engineering from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and a master’s degree in systems engineering from Johns Hopkins University. He will assume his duties at the laboratory as it approaches its 90th anniversary since being founded by Caltech.
